name: SESC 24 de Maio
key_features: Ramps wind up through a gutted department store to a new rooftop pool and terrace above downtown.

name: Teatro General San Martín
key_features: Glass curtain wall fronting several stacked auditoriums and a public lobby opening onto the avenue.

name: Palacio Salvo
key_features: Eclectic concrete tower with a stepped crown, the twin of Buenos Aires' Palacio Barolo, on the main square.

name: Toba Sea-Folk Museum
key_features: Long tiled-roof storehouses and laminated-timber exhibition halls built for a humid, salty coast.

name: Temple of Heaven
key_features: Triple-roofed circular timber hall on a three-tier marble terrace, reached by a raised axial walkway.

name: Hong Kong City Hall
key_features: Low and high blocks linked by a memorial garden court, with a clean concrete frame and glazing.

name: Morpheus Hotel
key_features: A free-form steel exoskeleton braces a tower pierced by three voids through its centre.

name: Lanyang Museum
key_features: A tilted wedge rising like the coast's cuesta rocks, clad in varied stone and glass panels.

name: Taipei Performing Arts Center
key_features: Three theatres plug into a central cube, with a public loop route running through the backstage.

name: Leeum, Samsung Museum of Art
key_features: Three buildings on a slope: a terracotta-clad inverted cone, rusted steel and glass boxes, black concrete.

name: National Gallery Singapore
key_features: Two colonial courts joined under a perforated metal canopy on tree-like columns, with a roof bridge.

name: Pinnacle@Duxton
key_features: Seven 50-storey public housing towers linked by continuous sky gardens on the 26th and 50th floors.

name: Kuala Lumpur International Airport
key_features: Repeated shell roof modules on tapered columns with skylights, and a rainforest planted inside.

name: Robot Building
key_features: A bank office styled as a robot, with eyes, antennae and bolt-like discs on its stepped facade.

name: Sirius Building
key_features: Stacked concrete units step and stagger above The Rocks, giving flats terraces and harbour views.

name: One Central Park
key_features: Vertical gardens climb two towers; a cantilevered heliostat redirects sunlight into the shaded park.

name: Helsinki Central Station
key_features: Granite station with a clock tower and lamp-bearing figures framing a vaulted main hall.

name: Slovak Radio Building
key_features: Inverted steel-framed pyramid of offices standing on its point above a base of studios.

name: Partisan Memorial Cemetery
key_features: Terraced paths and retaining walls of cut stone climb a hillside, with tombstones set along the levels.

name: IIT Kanpur Academic Area
key_features: Lecture halls, labs and library in brick and concrete joined by a continuous covered walkway system.

name: Government Museum and Art Gallery
key_features: Brick-clad gallery block on a concrete frame, a version of the square museum of unlimited growth.

name: Indian Coffee House
key_features: A cylindrical brick tower with a ramp of tables spiralling up inside perforated jali walls.

name: Rock Garden of Chandigarh
key_features: Outdoor rooms and passages built from broken ceramics, rubble and scrap, linked by narrow paths.

name: Mazar-e-Quaid
key_features: A white marble cube with pointed arches and a shallow dome, raised on a platform in a large park.

name: Patan Museum
key_features: Galleries fitted into a restored Malla palace wing around its courtyard, with discreet new structure.

name: Hilton Istanbul
key_features: A slab on pilotis with a honeycomb of deep balconies facing the Bosphorus, entered under a wavy canopy.

name: King Abdullah Petroleum Studies and Research Center
key_features: Hexagonal cells grow from a honeycomb grid, with shaded facades and courtyards against the desert sun.

name: Education City Mosque
key_features: A prayer hall raised on five columns over a water garden, with two calligraphy-clad minarets.

name: Le Corbusier Gymnasium
key_features: A concrete sports hall with a sloping roof and a wall that opens toward outdoor tiered seating.

name: New Baris
key_features: Mud-brick vaults and domes with wind catchers and underground air ducts for an unfinished desert market.

name: Nubia Museum
key_features: Sandstone and granite volumes stepped into a hillside, with an outdoor garden of Nubian houses and water.

name: University of Constantine
key_features: A long concrete classroom slab on few supports beside a curved auditorium and a tall prismatic tower.

name: Maqam Echahid
key_features: Three tall concrete palm fronds meet at the top to shelter an eternal flame above a museum.

name: Kamalapur railway station
key_features: Row of thin concrete umbrella shells forms a shading canopy over an open concourse.

name: Gate of Europe
key_features: Twin office towers leaning 15 degrees towards each other across a square.

name: SEC Armadillo
key_features: Overlapping aluminium-clad shells over an auditorium beside the Clyde.

name: Thyssen-Bornemisza Museum
key_features: Palace rebuilt inside around top-lit galleries and a central double-height hall.

name: Nanjing International Youth Cultural Centre
key_features: Two towers and a conference podium blend into one continuous flowing ribbon at the base.

name: New Orleans Tower
key_features: A slender stone-clad residential tower rising from a low base that houses a cinema.

name: Generali Tower
key_features: Floor plates rotate progressively up the tower, giving it a twisting glass profile.

name: Sanctuary of Meritxell
key_features: Arcaded stone walls with tall arched openings recall regional Romanesque forms.

name: Roche Tower (Bau 1)
key_features: A stepped tower whose setbacks form terraces, with white horizontal bands shading the glazing.

name: Place Ville Marie
by: I. M. Pei, Henry N. Cobb
key_features: Cruciform office tower over a plaza and shopping concourse that began the city's underground network.

name: Tour de la Bourse
key_features: Tower with tapering concrete corner columns and recessed mechanical floors dividing the shaft.

name: Kyushu National Museum
key_features: Undulating roof over a glass-walled hall that reflects the wooded hillside.

name: Muziekgebouw aan 't IJ
key_features: Glass box on the IJ waterfront around a concert hall, under a large overhanging roof.

name: Tokyo Sea Life Park
key_features: Glass dome entrance rises behind a pool whose edge merges with the sea horizon of Tokyo Bay.

name: Tour Perret
key_features: Early concrete residential tower expressing its frame over the rebuilt station square.

name: World Forum (Congress Building)
key_features: Congress hall and triangular tower with facades of coloured tiles.

name: Rohm Theatre Kyoto
key_features: Deep concrete eaves and a forecourt plaza tie the halls together; renovated keeping the shell.

name: Raffles City Chongqing
key_features: A horizontal glass skybridge conservatory about 300 m long rests across four towers.

name: Zorlu Center
key_features: Mixed-use complex of homes, offices, shops and a performing arts centre around open terraces.

name: Torre BBVA Mexico
key_features: Diagonally braced tower behind a patterned solar screen, with sky gardens up its height.

name: The Lighthouse (Glasgow Herald Building)
key_features: Former newspaper offices with a corner water-tower turret, converted into a design centre.

name: Tokyo Skytree
key_features: Triangular base morphs into a round plan, with a concrete core acting as a pagoda-style damping column.

name: Yokosuka Museum of Art
key_features: Glass outer skin over a steel box with round openings, partly sunk into a slope above the bay.

name: Svaneke Water Tower
key_features: Tapering concrete tank volume raised on legs above a small harbour town.

name: Estadio Universitario de Caracas
key_features: Baseball stands sheltered by a thin cantilevered concrete canopy free of columns.

name: Žižkov Television Tower
key_features: Three steel-clad concrete shafts carry pods for antennas, a restaurant and viewing decks.

name: White House (Moscow)
key_features: Marble-clad tower over a wide stepped base set on the bank of the Moskva river.

name: King Power Mahanakhon
key_features: Glass tower cut by a spiralling pixelated band of cantilevered boxes and terraces.

name: Grieg Hall
key_features: Glass-fronted foyer wedge facing the city, in front of a concrete concert hall.

name: Joensuu Town Hall
key_features: Red brick town hall and theatre combined in one block under a tall tower.

name: London Central Mosque
key_features: Golden dome over a square prayer hall beside a slender minaret, facing Regent's Park.

name: State Kremlin Palace
key_features: Glass and marble slab partly sunk into the ground to stay low among the Kremlin buildings.

name: European Investment Bank
key_features: Glass vaulted envelope over V-shaped office wings and winter gardens.

name: SIS Building
key_features: Stepped ziggurat of green glass and cream panels terracing down to the Thames.

name: Kaknas Tower
key_features: Square concrete shaft carrying a stacked head of equipment and viewing floors.

name: National Palace of Culture
key_features: Massive multi-hall congress building set at the end of a long landscaped park axis.

name: Te Papa Tongarewa
key_features: Plan split along an axis between Maori and Pakeha halves, with the building on base isolators.

name: Fix Brewery (National Museum of Contemporary Art)
key_features: Former brewery with long horizontal bands of concrete and glazing, converted into galleries.

name: Sava Centar
key_features: Large congress complex with dark glazed curtain walls wrapping a main hall of about 4,000 seats.

name: Leopold Museum
key_features: White limestone cube with a central glazed atrium inside the MuseumsQuartier.

name: Las Lajas Sanctuary
key_features: Gothic Revival church set on an arched bridge across a river gorge, its altar against the cliff.

name: İstanbul Modern
key_features: A museum raised on slender columns with a reflective panelled skin and a public terrace on the Bosphorus.

name: Florya Atatürk Marine Mansion
key_features: A modernist summer house built on piles over the sea, reached by a pier from the shore.

name: Palace of Serbia
key_features: H-shaped federal government block around a central domed ceremonial hall.

name: Museum of the Future
key_features: Torus of steel and glass panels on a diagrid frame, with calligraphy forming the windows.

name: Peak Tower
key_features: Bowl-shaped roof raised on piers over the Peak Tram terminus, read against the ridge line.

name: Red Banner Textile Factory
key_features: Factory power station shaped as a massive sculpted block with horizontal window bands.

name: Shakespeare's Globe
key_features: Reconstructed open-air timber-frame theatre with a thatched roof and lime plaster.

name: Museum of Modern Art in Warsaw
key_features: Plain white concrete block with large windows onto a city square, and simple galleries.

name: Wales Millennium Centre
key_features: Bronze-coloured steel shell and stacked Welsh slate bands, with poetry cut into the facade.

name: Musée Hergé
key_features: Coloured gallery volumes around a top-lit atrium crossed by footbridges, like panels of a comic strip.

name: Grand Théâtre de Québec
key_features: Massive concrete block with a sculpted concrete mural wrapping the lobby walls.

name: Israel Goldstein Synagogue
key_features: A white shell dome lifted on arched supports above an open ground floor on the campus.

name: Matenadaran
key_features: A basalt manuscript archive with a deep arched portal set into the hill above a statue-lined stair.

name: Four Seasons Centre for the Performing Arts
key_features: Glass foyer with a free-spanning glass stair, wrapped around a horseshoe hall on isolation pads.

name: José Martí Memorial
key_features: Tower on a five-pointed star plan rising over the Plaza de la Revolucion.

name: Pointe-à-Callière Museum
key_features: Museum built over excavated foundations of the first settlement, shown in a crypt below the street.

name: St. Paul's Cathedral, Abidjan
key_features: A leaning tower, read as a stylised figure of the saint, holds the nave roof with stays.

name: Sansad Bhavan (Old Parliament House)
key_features: Circular building ringed by an open colonnade of 144 columns around its chambers.

name: Ontario Science Centre
key_features: Three buildings stepped down a ravine and joined by bridges and escalators.

name: Union Buildings
key_features: Two office wings joined by a semicircular colonnade framing an amphitheatre above terraced gardens.

name: Villa Isola
key_features: Symmetrical curved wings step down the slope on an axis aimed at the volcano to the north.

name: Royal Exhibition Building
key_features: Great exhibition hall on a cross-shaped plan of nave and transepts meeting under a dome.

name: Sacred Heart Cathedral, Casablanca
key_features: Reinforced concrete church translating Gothic verticality into Art Deco buttresses and pierced screens.

name: State Library Victoria
key_features: Octagonal reading room under a reinforced concrete dome, with desks radiating from the centre.

name: Fort Jesus
key_features: Bastioned Renaissance fort of coral stone, its plan laid out like a human figure on a coastal ridge.

name: Old Government Buildings
key_features: Very large timber building detailed to imitate stone, built in wood for earthquake resilience.
